_meta.source: Hand-authored for this repo (Week 8), grounded in real LINDDUN Pro threat-tree nodes -- NOT transcribed from an external human-authored assignment or an authoritative third-party report. Weaker evidentiary status than KidsTube (human HW2) or Genomic (NIST SP 1800-43C) until independently reviewed. Same caveat as family_location's gold standard.
_meta.field_notes: dfd_source_id/dfd_destination_id anchor each threat to a real dfd.json flow (location-based matching, same convention as Genomic/family_location -- see eval/match.py's flow_anchored = scenario == 'kidstube' check). All flows are Process-mediated, so every threat is structurally reachable.

threats.title: Static guest unlock codes link every entry by the same guest across visits
threats.description: Guest unlock codes are not rotated per visit, so every entry event using the same code can be linked together into a single guest's visit history, even if the guest's real identity is otherwise unknown to the system.
threats.assumptions: Guest access codes are reused across multiple visits rather than generated fresh each time.

threats.title: Guest access codes stored/transmitted without encryption
threats.description: Similar to KidsTube's JWT-in-localStorage pattern, temporary guest unlock codes are stored and transmitted to the Home Hub without encryption, so anyone intercepting local traffic or accessing the Hub's storage can capture a currently-valid code.
threats.assumptions: No evidence of end-to-end encryption for the guest-code enrollment/verification path.

threats.title: Local event log retains motion/door/lock events indefinitely with no automatic purge
threats.description: The Local Event Log accumulates every sensor, door, and lock event indefinitely with no automatic deletion or archival policy, well beyond what active security monitoring requires.
threats.assumptions: No retention/lifecycle job or documented deletion policy was found for the Local Event Log.

threats.title: Full-resolution continuous video is stored rather than motion-triggered snippets only
threats.description: The Home Hub uploads full-resolution, continuously-recorded video clips to cloud storage rather than only the shorter motion-triggered snippets that the stated security purpose requires, retaining substantially more footage volume than necessary.
threats.assumptions: Cameras record continuously rather than only during a detected motion/door event window.

threats.title: Cloud video storage credentials are shared/hardcoded, exposing the entire video archive if compromised
threats.description: Credentials or API keys used by the Home Hub to upload to Cloud Video Storage are hardcoded in firmware or reused across the homeowner's other cloud services; if leaked, they expose the entire historical video archive, not just a single clip.
threats.assumptions: No evidence of per-device, rotatable, least-privilege credentials for the video-upload path.

threats.node_remap_note: Cited D.1.1 until 2026-07-28. That node was invented by this project's Week 1 RECONSTRUCTION of the LINDDUN trees and does not exist in the official trees (v241203, bundled at references/linddun-trees/). Retargeted to the official D.1 (Observed communications); threat content unchanged.
threats.title: Unencrypted local-to-cloud traffic reveals occupancy timing via traffic analysis alone
threats.description: An adversary monitoring network traffic between the Home Hub and the Mobile App Backend can detect exactly when motion alerts fire -- and infer when the home is occupied or empty -- purely from traffic timing and volume, without decrypting the payload.
threats.assumptions: No evidence that Hub-to-backend traffic is encrypted or padded to obscure event timing.

threats.title: Push notification metadata leaks room-level occupancy patterns without opening the app
threats.description: Someone with access to push-notification metadata (e.g. a shared family phone, or a compromised notification-service integration) can infer which room or entry point triggered an alert based on which notification template fired, without ever opening the app or accessing raw sensor data.
threats.assumptions: Notification templates are camera/sensor-specific (e.g. "front door" vs. a generic alert) rather than uniformly worded.

threats.title: Aggregating motion/door events across all sensors builds a detailed occupancy profile
threats.description: Combining motion, door, and lock events across all of the homeowner's sensors over time reveals a detailed occupancy profile -- when they leave for work, when they're away for extended periods -- well beyond what any single sensor's individual event implies.
threats.assumptions: Historical events across all sensors are jointly queryable, not siloed per device.

threats.title: "Aggregated" usage analytics shared with the vendor can be re-linked into household-level profiles
threats.description: Usage analytics shared with the third-party analytics vendor, though described as aggregated and non-identifying, can be combined with the vendor's other data sources (device/session identifiers, timing patterns) to reconstruct household-level behavioral profiles.
threats.assumptions: The analytics payload includes device- or session-level identifiers rather than only fully aggregated, k-anonymized statistics.

Retargeted to the official Nc.1.2 (Generic regulatory noncompliance); threat content unchanged.
threats.title: Analytics sharing with the third-party vendor is on by default with no explicit consent screen
threats.description: Sharing usage analytics with the third-party analytics vendor is on by default; the homeowner is never shown an explicit, purpose-specific consent screen distinguishing it from the core security-monitoring functionality during setup.
threats.assumptions: The privacy policy discloses third-party sharing in general terms but the app has no dedicated consent toggle shown during onboarding.

threats.title: No technical or contractual control over the analytics vendor's downstream use for targeted advertising
threats.description: Once usage analytics reach the third-party vendor, the platform has no enforced technical or contractual control preventing that vendor from repurposing the data for targeted advertising or reselling it to downstream ad-tech intermediaries.
threats.assumptions: Any data-sharing agreement with the analytics vendor is not technically enforced (e.g. no data-use audit or deletion-on-request mechanism).

threats.title: Guests are never shown any notice that their entry/exit is being logged and retained
threats.description: Guests receiving a temporary unlock code are never shown any notice -- at the door, in an app, or otherwise -- that their entry and exit events are being logged and retained by the system.
threats.assumptions: The guest-code flow has no notice or acknowledgment step beyond entering the code.

threats.node_remap_note: Cited U.1.3 until 2026-07-28. That node was invented by this project's Week 1 RECONSTRUCTION of the LINDDUN trees and does not exist in the official trees (v241203, bundled at references/linddun-trees/). Retargeted to the official U.1.1 (Unawareness as data subject); threat content unchanged.
threats.title: Disclosures don't specify how long footage/logs are retained or exactly which third parties receive analytics
threats.description: The privacy policy and in-app disclosures describe data collection in general terms but do not specify a concrete retention period for video footage or event logs, nor precisely which third parties receive usage analytics beyond a generic "analytics partners" reference.
threats.assumptions: No specific retention duration or itemized third-party recipient list is published in the homeowner-facing privacy documentation.

threats.title: Retrieved video clips carry timestamped metadata directly identifying who appears on camera
threats.description: Video clips retrieved for playback include timestamp and device metadata that directly identifies which household member (or guest) appears on camera at a given time, with no on-device redaction or blurring option before playback or export.
threats.assumptions: Clip metadata and playback include full timestamp/location context with no built-in redaction feature.

threats.title: Cloud-stored clips retain device serial numbers and account identifiers that re-identify the homeowner if leaked
threats.description: Cloud-stored video clips retain embedded device serial numbers and account identifiers in their metadata, so a leaked or improperly shared clip can be traced back to the homeowner's account even without any explicit identity label on the footage itself.
threats.assumptions: Uploaded clips are not stripped of device/account metadata before storage.

threats.title: Every guest entry is permanently logged with an attributable timestamp
threats.description: Every guest entry via a temporary code is permanently logged with a timestamp attributable to that specific code, creating a persistent record that could later be used as evidence against the guest (e.g. in a dispute) without their awareness that such a record exists.
threats.assumptions: Entry logs are retained indefinitely and are not disclosed to the guest at the time of entry.

threats.title: Motion alerts are irrevocably attributed to a sensor/timestamp with no way to dispute a false positive
threats.description: Motion alerts forwarded from the Home Hub to the backend are irrevocably attributed to a specific sensor and timestamp, with no mechanism for the homeowner to later annotate or dispute a false-positive alert as inaccurate once it has been logged.
threats.assumptions: The alert pipeline has no correction/annotation feature after an alert is generated and stored.

threats.title: No documented data-minimization review for continuous video/audio capture relative to the security purpose
threats.description: The system has no documented data-minimization review assessing whether the volume and continuity of video/audio capture is proportionate to the stated home-security purpose, a data-protection principle expected of continuous-surveillance consumer devices.
threats.assumptions: No DPIA or data-minimization documentation was found for the camera/sensor capture configuration.
